messages:
sam: Proposal: 6-week pilot to tighten postmortem follow-ups and enforce remediation ownership. Aim: reduce recurrence of same failure modes + speed closure. Thoughts?

elena: 👍 good. Can we start with a tiny template + clear SLAs? e.g., assign RCA owner within 24h, remediation owner within 72h, 2-week interim check-ins.

devon: Agree. Also propose rotating IC every 2 weeks so more folks know the play. cc @marco on runbook changes.

sam: Rotation idea makes sense. Need to document handoff checklist. Minimal: ownership, current hypothesis, open actions, contacts.

elena: Draft timeline template:

```
Day 0: Incident triage + bridge
Day 0-1: RCA owner assigned, initial notes
Day 1-3: Postmortem draft + interim remediation scope
Day 3-7: Remediation owner assigned, high-priority fixes scheduled
Week 2: First remediation checkpoint (status + blockers)
Week 4: Mid-pilot review (metrics on recurrence/cost)
Week 6: Closure review + lessons learned, update runbooks
``` 

marco: LGTM. Can we add a 'recurrence signal' field so we tag if it's similar to past incidents? Maybe a quick cosine-sim on titles/metrics would help prioritize.

devon: Yes. Also add 'priority of remediation' based on recurrence and customer impact. That provides routing for dedicated capacity or hotfix.

sam: @tina can you own pilot logistics? If yes, please propose weekly sync cadence and invite list.

tina: I can. Suggest weekly 30m triage + biweekly 1hr remediation review. Invite: RCA owner, remediation owner, infra oncall, PM (if customer-impacting).

incident-bot: incident-bot added label `postmortem-pilot` to INCIDENT-2026-307

elena: Also want a simple tracking sheet (Google) with columns: incident id, owner, remediation owner, due date, status, recurrence flag, last updated. I'll drop a template in #docs once Tina confirms cadence.

sam: Cool. Next: starting Monday. Tina to send invite + link to tracking sheet. We'll run 6 weeks then reassess. :rocket:

devon: :thumbsup: Will pull historical incidents for recurrence-signal rules. Ping if you want a quick script.
